clue.text: The very best speed limit

definitions.meaning: first-class, of the highest grade or quality
the maximum pace allowed or possible

explanation.surface: Someone praises the finest possible maximum speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-rate is an adjective for first-class, and the top rate of something such as speed is its ceiling.

clue.text: Mattress case removed and put on the mat

parts.note: ticking or tick is the strong fabric case of a mattress
off means taken away

explanation.surface: A mattress cover is taken off and laid on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the mat' is an idiom for being called before a superior for a reprimand.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold someone is to carpet them, an idiom for a reprimand.

clue.text: He offers correct ready-let transfer

parts.note: proper means correct

indicators.note: moving these letters about gives a new order

explanation.surface: An estate agent offers proper flats already let for transfer.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate agent is someone who puts houses up for sale or rent.

clue.text: Copy mystery man if you want a tip

parts.note: to ape is to imitate
X stands for an unknown person, as in Mr X

explanation.surface: Advice to imitate an enigmatic stranger for a hint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like advice but means a peak.
explanation.definitionFit: A summit or highest point is the pointed top of something.

clue.text: Returned book I have found passion rousing

indicators.note: sent back, so the word for a volume is read from its end

parts.note: a tome is a large book
I've, contracted

explanation.surface: Someone returns a library book and finds it stirring.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotive means stirring strong feeling, arousing the emotions.

clue.text: Ancient habit which puts an end to Saratoga

indicators.note: the wanted letters form the closing stretch of the place name, so they end it

explanation.surface: An old style of dress is said to have finished off the town of Saratoga.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' means clothing here, as in a riding habit; the Roman garment ends the word Saratoga.
explanation.definitionFit: Habit can mean costume, and the Romans wore this draped robe in antiquity.

clue.text: Equatorial shipping company

definitions.meaning: concerning the equator, which sailors call this when crossing it
a fleet operator, a named shipping line

explanation.surface: A cruise operator sailing near the equator.
explanation.walkthrough: Sailors speak of 'crossing the line' for crossing the equator.
explanation.definitionFit: Mariners name the equator this, and a steamship company is a line.

clue.text: Crazy Georgia twins

indicators.note: a pair of identical copies, so the abbreviation appears twice

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: Some twins from Georgia are mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga is slang for mad or senile.

clue.text: Formula for output of mine invested by the others

indicators.note: to be invested is to be surrounded, so one piece is wrapped by the other

parts.note: them, the other people
ore is what a mine produces

explanation.surface: A formula for the production of a pit run by other people.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem is a proposition proved by reasoning, often stated as a mathematical formula.

clue.text: Sounds as though slave was sold, healed, and newly shod

indicators.note: what is said aloud matches the spoken words that follow

parts.note: a slave sold and then cured: sold and healed

explanation.surface: A grim auction: a slave sold, nursed back to health and given new shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'sold and healed' matches the phrase for having new soles and heels fitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitted with new soles and heels means freshly reshod, figuratively well off.

clue.text: Got in a pickle and prepared Christmas dinner

definitions.meaning: ruined one's own prospects, landed in trouble
roasted the festive bird, traditionally a goose in Britain

explanation.surface: A cook gets into a mess while making the festive meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means spoiled someone's chances, while literally roasting a goose was the old Christmas meal.

clue.text: In Australia the old cry…

indicators.note: one word placed within the other, the old form going inside the country

parts.note: Oz is the informal name for Australia
ye is an archaic spelling of the definite article

explanation.surface: An old call heard down under.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into the next one with an ellipsis, but each is solved separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A court crier or town crier calls this word to demand silence and attention.

clue.text: … of the town which may be re-echoed

indicators.note: a word that comes back the same when sent back from the far end reads identically in both directions

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Continuing the town crier: something municipal that echoes around.
explanation.definitionFit: Civic is an adjective meaning relating to a city or municipality.

clue.text: Carry Put Options would be his advice

definitions.meaning: to support or transport

definitions.text: Put Options would be his advice
definitions.meaning: a stock-market speculator expecting prices to fall would recommend buying put options

explanation.surface: A financial adviser recommends put options to carry a client.
explanation.walkthrough: On the stock exchange a bear expects prices to fall, and put options profit from a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a load is to transport it, and a market pessimist is called a bear.

clue.text: Sprightly though time is about 1.50

indicators.note: surrounds, so the time word goes round the numerals

parts.note: an age is a period of time
1 is I and 50 is L in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone is nimble despite a time of about a minute fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: '1.50' looks like a time or price but is read as Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Agile means nimble, able to move quickly and lightly.

clue.text: Shoot a young aristocrat

definitions.meaning: a cutting or twig from a plant
a descendant of a noble family

explanation.surface: Someone is told to shoot a young nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A scion is both a plant cutting for grafting and an heir of a noble house.

clue.text: Result of shattering ague fit

indicators.note: breaking these two words into pieces lets their letters be rebuilt

explanation.surface: A bout of fever leaves someone utterly worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shattering' does two things: it rearranges AGUE FIT, and a shattering bout of fever leaves you exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhaustion is what follows a draining attack of fever.

clue.text: Blurt out a demand for alimony?

definitions.meaning: cry out suddenly
read as ..., a claim made by a former spouse

explanation.surface: A divorcee shouts out a demand for maintenance payments.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: an ex's claim is a demand for alimony.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry out suddenly is to shout an interjection, and the second reading splits into former partner plus demand.

clue.text: He plays or maybe he plays around with things

definitions.meaning: a violinist, a player of the fiddle

definitions.text: maybe he plays around with things
definitions.meaning: someone who tinkers or cheats

explanation.surface: A musician who also tinkers with everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A violinist plays, and someone who fidgets or cheats on accounts also earns the name.

clue.text: Chumpy cheeked chump

parts.note: a fool with a plump face: chubby cheeks make a plump head, and a plump head is slang for an idiot

explanation.surface: A round-faced fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Chump is also slang for the head, so a fleshy-cheeked chump is literally a fleshy head.
explanation.definitionFit: A fathead is a stupid person, a dolt.

clue.text: Leave drunk to talk parrot fashion

definitions.meaning: stagger away unsteadily
recite rapidly from memory

explanation.surface: A tipsy guest departs while chattering mindlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger away is to lurch off, and to rattle off a list from memory is the idiom.

clue.text: Showed politeness to a lady but not to date

definitions.meaning: rose to one's feet when a woman entered, an old courtesy
failed to turn up for a date

explanation.surface: A man is courteous to a woman but lets down his date.
explanation.definitionFit: Rising for a lady is old-fashioned manners; jilting someone by not appearing is the other sense.

clue.text: Travesties with which South Africa gets bored

parts.note: tires means grows weary

explanation.surface: Mockeries that leave South Africa weary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bored' suggests drilling but here means wearied.
explanation.definitionFit: Satires and travesties both mock their subject by grotesque imitation.

clue.text: Frenchman who painted a young chick

definitions.meaning: Nicolas ..., seventeenth-century French classical painter
a very young chicken bred for eating

explanation.surface: A French painter depicted a baby bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicolas Poussin was a French artist, and the French word for a spring chicken is also used in English cookery.

clue.text: Some turn to gin

indicators.note: turning the word for a portion around reads it from the end

parts.note: part means some, a portion

explanation.surface: Someone takes up drinking spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin' is not the drink but a snare, as in a cotton gin or a rabbit gin.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is an old word for a snare used to catch animals.

clue.text: Their model BBC director general

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone held up as a role model for the BBC's chief.
explanation.walkthrough: John REITH was the first director general of the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Reith founded and led the British Broadcasting Corporation as its first chief.

clue.text: Boy friend giving a pronounced bow

indicators.note: spoken, so the word is the one that sounds alike

parts.note: a bow as in a ribbon tied in loops, rhyming with go

explanation.surface: A boyfriend makes a showy bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' must be said to rhyme with 'go', not 'cow'.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is an old-fashioned word for a male suitor.

clue.text: In the middle of last year it was an eyesore

indicators.note: the letters are found spanning the centre of the two words

explanation.surface: Something ugly turned up in mid-way through the previous year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eyesore' reads as an ugly sight but is a sore on the eyelid.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, literally a sore eye.

clue.text: A rising island by a large continent

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the letters read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: An island rising up beside a huge landmass.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest of the world's continents.

clue.text: Are they enough to silence Ulster disturbance?

definitions.text: Are they enough to silence Ulster disturbance?

indicators.note: disorder applied to the words before it scrambles their letters

explanation.surface: Asks whether polling outcomes can quieten unrest in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbance' rearranges TO SILENCE ULSTER, and the whole clue asks whether a vote can end the troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: Polling outcomes might settle political unrest, the hope the clue voices.

clue.text: Sort of knot sailors steer clear of

definitions.meaning: a square knot used for tying sails
a ridge of rock or coral near the surface

explanation.surface: A type of knot that sailors avoid.
explanation.definitionFit: A square knot for shortening sail shares its name with a hazardous ridge of rock.

clue.text: Substitute for sand mixed in tin

indicators.note: the two words are stirred together, their letters combined in a new order

explanation.surface: Sand blended into tin as a replacement material.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in is a replacement who takes another's place.
